`moveEnter` plays once. When an element should move **between states** — selected, expanded, loading, in error — bind the state and let the animation follow it. There are two reactive APIs; both are stable.

## One element, one computed target: `moveAnimation`

[`MoveAnimationDirective`](/docs/reference/move-animation-directive) takes a single `initial`, `animate` and `exit` state and animates whenever `animate` changes. It compares the state by value, so an object literal in the template does not replay on every change-detection pass. Only properties present in **both** `initial` and `animate` are animated.

:::code card-state.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-card-state',
  imports: [MoveAnimationDirective],
  template: `
    <button type="button" (click)="open.set(!open())">Toggle</button>

    <div
      [moveAnimation]="{
        initial: { opacity: 0.6, scale: 0.98 },
        animate: open() ? { opacity: 1, scale: 1 } : { opacity: 0.6, scale: 0.98 },
      }"
    >
      Card
    </div>
  `,
})
export class CardState {
  protected readonly open = signal(false);
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/variants.ts#L5-L23)

## Named states: `moveVariants`

Use [`MoveVariantsDirective`](/docs/reference/move-variants-directive) when states have names, a whole subtree shares the active variant, or you want `staggerChildren` and `delayChildren`. Set the active variant with `moveVariant`.

:::code selectable.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-selectable',
  imports: [MoveVariantsDirective],
  template: `
    <div
      [moveVariants]="{
        idle: { scale: 1, rotate: 0 },
        active: { scale: 1.08, rotate: 4 },
      }"
      [moveVariant]="selected() ? 'active' : 'idle'"
      moveDuration="200ms"
    >
      Card
    </div>
  `,
})
export class Selectable {
  protected readonly selected = signal(false);
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/variants.ts#L27-L45)

::playground[variants]

> [!WARNING]
> On a host with `moveVariants`, set the state with `moveVariant` (or its alias `moveActiveVariant`) — not `moveAnimate`, which `moveVariants` takes over.

## Which one?

| You have…                                 | Use                         |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| One element and a computed target         | `moveAnimation`             |
| Named states, shared by a subtree         | `moveVariants`              |
| A boolean that plays forward and reverses | `moveTarget` (experimental) |

[Choose an API](/docs/api-selection) has the full comparison, including which directives are one-shot.

**Related:** [`moveAnimation` playground](/demos/animation) · [`moveVariants` playground](/demos/variants) · [`moveTarget` playground](/demos/target) (experimental)
